title: The Visitor Who Stayed a Season

collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — DEPARTURES AND EXILE (DEP-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Leaving and being left: moving huts, short journeys, visitors going home, goodbyes done well and badly, homesickness, and the rare person who sails away for good. Choosing to leave is never a rejection of one's people, and choosing to stay is never a failure.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks an adult)

collection.description: A traveler who has stayed a whole season wants to leave but dreads the goodbyes: help them say goodbye, or let them go quietly.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: A traveler who came for one night has now stayed a whole season. Everyone likes them. They help in the gardens and tell good stories. But lately (name1) has noticed them standing on the beach in the evenings, looking along the coast, and today they say, with some difficulty, "I think I should go. I just don't know how to say goodbye to everybody."

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: "You don't have to say goodbye to everybody," says (name1). "Say it to me, and I'll tell them." The traveler hugs (him/her) and leaves before the village wakes. (name1) spends the day telling people. Some are sad. A few are cross not to have been told. All of them, by evening, are telling their favorite of the traveler's stories.

o1__fx.name: Outcome A
o1__fx.text: (name1) suggests a small fire on their last night, nothing big. The traveler agrees. Half the village turns up anyway. There are speeches, and a song, and a very large fish. The traveler cries, and laughs, and leaves at dawn carrying more food than they can possibly eat.
